newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end lower, seen steadying.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end lower, seen steadying.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa continued its downward trend on follow-through selling Monday but was seen on the verge of bottoming out, dealers said.

"Prices are still falling from the inertia of recent profit-taking, but they should soon level out unless (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins speech jolts the markets," one dealer said.
Greenspan speaks before Congress Tuesday and Wednesday.
The blue-chip MerVal index fell 1.4 percent to 790.70, extending last week's 5.7 percent dive which traders blamed on fears of a devaluation in Brazil.
"The market may keep falling but it will soon enter a range where it is convenient to buy, as least for short-term speculative purposes," said analyst Rodrigo Diz at traders Velox investments.
"Medium-term, we may enter a neutral period ahead of October (midterm) elections where any good news is offset by political jitters," he added.

Diz also claimed strong protests against the government last Friday marking the third anniversary of the bombing of the AMIA Jewish center, which killed 86 people and has not yet been clarified, helped to dampen sentiment on the markets.
Floor volume shrank to 22.6 million pesos from 27.4 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover slowed to 78.5 million pesos.
The broad market closed off 1.8 percent, with losers smashing winners 56 to six and six issues closing flat.
The only main-tier gainer was business conglomerate Comercial del Plata, which rose 0.9 percent.
Heaviest MerVal losers were carmaker Ciadea, which tumbled 3.4 percent, Banco Frances and Telecom, both down 3.2 percent, and foods giant Molinos, off 2.7 percent.
